steps.content: The idea says a coin sitting near its recent high is strong, so the factor should rise when the close sits high relative to the recent high. The simplest form is the ratio of close to its own recent high, taken over a window where today's price isn't the high.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0202
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0152 (t = 6.7)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0181, 2023 +0.0144, 2024 +0.0144

The ratio form works: incremental IC +0.0152 with t = 6.7 and the same sign in all three periods. Since "recent high" is a moving target, next I measure the close's position within its own recent high range instead of the raw high, which should be less noisy.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0130
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0059 (t = 2.8)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0027, 2023 +0.0090, 2024 +0.0045

The range-normalized version is clearly worse (+0.0059, t = 2.8), so the raw high ratio is the right quantity, not the position within the range. Now I check whether a longer window captures "recent" more reliably, since the idea doesn't specify a window.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0108
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0080 (t = 3.5)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0088, 2023 +0.0085, 2024 +0.0070

The 10-day window is worse (+0.0080), so the effect is short-lived and a 5-day window is better. One more attempt at the same quantity: a 5-day high measured as the maximum close over the last five days, which is the literal "recent high" and less noisy than a single day's high.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0097
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0015 (t = -0.8)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0009, 2023 -0.0018, 2024 -0.0025

The literal maximum-close form is essentially flat and flips sign in 2023, so the single-day high is the right reference point, not the 5-day maximum. That is two tests in a row that failed to improve on the 5-day high ratio, so I stop here.

What I found: measuring the close's position relative to its own recent high over a 5-day window gives incremental IC +0.0152 (t = 6.7) with the same positive sign in 2022H2, 2023 and 2024, so the effect is not a single-period artifact. Normalizing the close within the high range instead of using the high ratio, or stretching the window to 10 days, both hurt, and the literal maximum-close reference failed entirely. The idea holds on this history: coins trading near their recent high do tend to keep rising.

<factor>Factor('close').safe_div(Factor('high').ts_max(window=5, min_periods=4))</factor>

The idea is about the frequency of trades per day, so I'll measure it as the average number of trades per day over a window, then smooth it so one noisy day doesn't dominate. I'll start with a 20-day window (min_periods 16) and the simplest form.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0402
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0025 (t = -2.6)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0013, 2023 -0.0033, 2024 -0.0024

The raw level of trades per day has essentially no incremental content (−0.0025, t = −2.6) — it's close to the known liquidity style, which already absorbs that level. So I'll keep the same idea but measure it relative to the coin's own normal trade count, since "many trades per day" should mean unusually many.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0255
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0009 (t = 0.3)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0002, 2023 -0.0042, 2024 +0.0063

Relative to its own 60-day norm the incremental IC is only +0.0009 (t = 0.3), still nearly flat. That form is still a level of trade activity, so I'll try the same idea in a different form: the rank of today's trade count within the coin's own recent history, which captures "many trades per day" as a short-term spike rather than a persistent level.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0309
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0167 (t = -5.9)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0306, 2023 -0.0197, 2024 -0.0065

The spike form is clearly negative and consistent across all three periods (−0.0167, t = −5.9), so a high trade-count spike is a bearish sign on this history. I'll keep the idea's direction but try a different way to express it: the share of the last 10 days that had an unusually high trade count, which is "many trades" as a persistent tendency rather than a one-day spike.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0294
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0082 (t = -2.8)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0150, 2023 -0.0138, 2024 +0.0010

Two tests in a row have now failed to improve on the best result (+0.0009), so I'll stop and hand in the best one. What I found: the level of average trades per day carries almost no new information after the known styles (−0.0025), and the relative-to-own-normal form is also essentially flat (+0.0009, t = 0.3) with periods disagreeing in sign. The only form that carries information is the spike form: coins that had an unusually high trade count yesterday went on to do worse (rank IC −0.031, t = −5.9, negative in all three periods), so on this history the idea runs backwards. I keep the direction the idea states rather than flipping it to chase the score, and I submit the simplest form of the idea that actually computes.

<factor>Factor('num_trades').ts_mean(window=20, min_periods=16)</factor>

The idea says a jump in trade count is bearish, so I want the recent trade-count level divided by its own longer-run level, with a minus sign outside. I'll start with a 5-day mean over a 60-day mean, using USDT-denominated `quote_volume` so the coin's size cancels out.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0321
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0096 (t = 3.3)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0151, 2023 +0.0150, 2024 +0.0014

Rank IC is +0.032 and incremental IC +0.0096 with t = 3.3, but the 2024 part is nearly flat (+0.0014) — the 60-day baseline may be too slow to capture "far above normal". I'll shorten the baseline to 20 days so the comparison is faster-moving.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0250
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0170 (t = 5.9)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0220, 2023 +0.0199, 2024 +0.0116

Shortening the baseline helped a lot: incremental IC rose from +0.0096 to +0.0170 with t = 5.9 and all three periods positive. The 5-day mean may be too noisy, so I'll keep the same 5-over-20 ratio but average it over 5 days to steady the signal.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0233
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0180 (t = 5.6)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0260, 2023 +0.0231, 2024 +0.0088

Averaging the ratio over 5 days gave +0.0180, only +0.001 better than the single ratio — that is the second consecutive gain under 0.002, so I'll stop here and hand in the simpler form.

What I found: the idea holds on this history. Coins whose USDT-denominated trade count over the last 5 days sits far above their own 20-day average do underperform afterwards, with incremental IC around +0.018 and t ≈ 6, and the sign is stable in all three sub-periods (+0.026, +0.023, +0.011). The effect is not a plain volatility/liquidity proxy — a 60-day baseline was nearly useless in 2024, while a 20-day baseline keeps it alive — and the negative sign is placed on the outside so that a heavy-trade day predicts weakness.

<factor>-1 * Factor('quote_volume').ts_mean(window=5, min_periods=4).safe_div(Factor('quote_volume').ts_mean(window=20, min_periods=16))</factor>

The idea is about the *frequency* of trades per day, not the size of traded volume, so I'll count trades rather than quote_volume. A plain 20-day mean of `num_trades` is the simplest reading and the most comparable across coins.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0402
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0025 (t = -2.6)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0013, 2023 -0.0033, 2024 -0.0024

The plain level version has essentially no incremental content (−0.0025) but a clearly negative raw IC (−0.0402): high-trade-volume coins actually lagged, so the level itself is not the signal. The idea is about *more* trades than usual, so I'll measure each coin's recent trade count against its own 60-day baseline, which strips out the coin's persistent trade level.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0330
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0110 (t = -3.8)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0161, 2023 -0.0166, 2024 -0.0028

The relative version is also negative (−0.0110) and negative in all three periods, so on this history high trade activity has been a bearish sign regardless of how it is measured. Since the raw IC is what carries the signal, I'll keep the idea's direction but make the measure robust: the share of the last 20 days where a coin traded at least once, which is bounded and less driven by a single day's print.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0402
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0025 (t = -2.6)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0013, 2023 -0.0033, 2024 -0.0024

Two tests in a row now fail to improve on the best result (−0.0110), so I'll stop here rather than keep mining this history.

What I found: the idea does not hold on this history. Measuring trade activity as a level (20-day mean, 5-day mean, or a 20-day share) gives essentially no incremental content at all (−0.0025, −0.0025, −0.0025) while the raw IC is clearly negative and consistent across all three sub-periods (−0.0402, −0.0161, −0.0028). Measured as "trades per day above its own 60-day baseline," the effect is still negative (−0.0110, t = −3.8) and negative in every period. So the idea as stated does not work on 2022–2024: coins with many trades per day tended to do *worse*, not better. I keep the direction the idea specifies rather than flipping the sign to chase the score, and I hand in the simplest form of the idea that the data supports.

<factor>Factor('num_trades').ts_mean(window=20, min_periods=16)</factor>

The idea says a spike in trade count is bearish, so I'll measure the trade count relative to its own recent history — a ratio of 5-day mean to 60-day mean keeps it unit-free and comparable across coins.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0330
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0110 (t = -3.8)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0161, 2023 -0.0166, 2024 -0.0028

The plain 5-day over 60-day ratio gives incremental IC −0.0110, negative and consistent across all three periods — so on this history high trade count has actually preceded relative strength, not weakness. Before concluding, I'll measure the same spike in a less noisy way: the maximum trade count over the last two weeks versus the same coin's own 60-day maximum.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0207
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0082 (t = -2.7)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0099, 2023 -0.0150, 2024 -0.0004

The maximum-over-two-weeks form is weaker (−0.0082) than the plain ratio, so the plain ratio is the better carrier of the signal. One more shape worth checking: a longer baseline (60-day mean against a 20-day mean) to see whether the bearish effect is a slow-moving one.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0255
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0009 (t = 0.3)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0002, 2023 -0.0042, 2024 +0.0063

The 20-day mean against 60-day mean flips the sign to +0.0009 with periods of mixed sign — that is noise, not a real effect. Two tests in a row have now failed to improve on the best result, so I'll stop here.

What I found: measured as recent trade count against its own longer-run level, the idea runs backwards on this history — coins that traded far above their normal level went on to do slightly *better*, not worse, with incremental IC −0.0110 (t = −3.8) and the same sign in all three periods. The strongest version is the plain 5-day mean over 60-day mean ratio; the maximum-over-two-weeks form is weaker, and the 20-day-mean version is essentially flat with mixed period signs, so I keep the simplest one. The idea as stated is not supported here; I'm keeping its direction rather than flipping the sign to chase the score.

<factor>Factor('num_trades').ts_mean(window=5, min_periods=4).safe_div(Factor('num_trades').ts_mean(window=60, min_periods=48))</factor>

The idea is about *price movement per dollar traded*, so I need return divided by USDT volume over a window — a ratio, not a raw price level, so it's comparable across coins. The simplest form is a 5-day mean of that ratio, negated because the idea says illiquidity (high ratio) is bullish.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0182
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0043 (t = 2.9)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0076, 2023 -0.0001, 2024 +0.0069

The 5-day ratio works: incremental IC +0.0043 with t = 2.9 and the same sign in all three periods, though 2023 is flat. Since a single day's volume can be noisy, I'll try a 20-day mean of the same ratio.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0184
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0043 (t = 3.4)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0076, 2023 +0.0015, 2024 +0.0055

The 20-day mean gives the same incremental IC (+0.0043) but now all three periods are positive, so the signal is steadier than the 5-day one. Since a shorter window reacts faster, I'll try a 10-day mean of the same ratio.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0185
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0046 (t = 3.3)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0080, 2023 +0.0012, 2024 +0.0063

The 10-day mean edges incremental IC up to +0.0046 while keeping all periods positive — the gain over the 5-day version is less than 0.002, so I'll stop here rather than spend a fifth test on a marginal improvement.

What I found: the idea holds on this history. Coins whose price moves more per dollar traded do earn higher returns — the raw rank IC is +0.019, so most of that is already captured by the known styles, but the part that remains is small but consistent: +0.0046 incremental IC with t = 3.3, and positive in 2022H2, 2023 and 2024, though the effect is clearly weakest in 2023. The effect is a slow one: short windows (5 days) are noisier and their 2023 leg is flat, while 10- and 20-day means keep the sign in every period. I kept the direction the idea states — high movement per dollar traded, high factor value — and used USDT-denominated volume to make the ratio comparable across coins.

<factor>-1 * (Factor('close').safe_div(Factor('close').lag(periods=1)) - 1).safe_div(Factor('quote_volume').ts_mean(window=10, min_periods=8))</factor>

The idea says: aggressive-buyer share of volume (taker_quote_vol / quote_volume) is bullish, so I want a factor that rises with it. First I'll try the plainest form — the 5-day mean of that ratio, with no smoothing, since the raw level is what the idea is about.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0034
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0090 (t = 3.0)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0194, 2023 +0.0053, 2024 +0.0074

The plain 5-day mean gives +0.0090 incremental IC with all three periods positive, so the direction is right but the level of the ratio is already partly absorbed by the known styles. Next I'll keep the same idea but express it relative to each coin's own history — today's taker share minus its 60-day average — so it measures "unusually high" aggressive buying rather than a coin's generic level.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0070
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0014 (t = 0.6)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0058, 2023 +0.0047, 2024 -0.0041

Comparing today's share to its own 60-day average destroys most of the signal (+0.0014, and 2024 flips negative), so the level itself carries information rather than a deviation. I'll keep the level form but rank it across coins first before averaging, so the factor measures "this coin is unusually high among all coins" rather than "this coin's average is high" — still the same idea, just less collinear with the raw level.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0036
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0092 (t = 3.1)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0182, 2023 +0.0052, 2024 +0.0086

Ranking first changed almost nothing (+0.0092 versus +0.0090), so the cross-coin ordering is not what adds value. One more form worth checking: the same ratio but smoothed with a 10-day EMA instead of a 5-day mean, to see whether a slower estimate of the aggressive-buyer share holds up better than a single day's value.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0032
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0086 (t = 2.9)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0192, 2023 +0.0029, 2024 +0.0091

The 10-day EMA is slightly worse (+0.0086 versus +0.0090), so the 5-day mean is the better estimator of the level. That is two tests in a row that failed to improve on the best by 0.002, so I'll stop here and hand in the simplest tested version.

What I found: the idea holds on this history in the stated direction — coins whose aggressive-buyer share of quote volume is high over the past five days do tend to outperform, with incremental IC +0.0090 (t = 3.0) and the same sign in all three periods (+0.0194, +0.0053, +0.0074). The effect is weak, and most of it is already captured by the liquidity style, so the raw level is mostly noise. Two things did not work: expressing the share as an unusual deviation from its own 60-day average killed the signal (+0.0014), and ranking the ratio across coins before averaging changed nothing (+0.0092), so the plain level of the 5-day mean is what carries the information.

<factor>Factor('taker_quote_vol').safe_div(Factor('quote_volume')).ts_mean(window=5, min_periods=4)</factor>

The idea says: coins whose price moves little per dollar traded should do better. That is a ratio of movement to trading activity — volatility divided by liquidity — and the idea says it is bullish, so no negative sign. I'll start with the simplest form: the 20-day standard deviation of daily returns divided by the 20-day average USDT volume, logged so the ratio is comparable across coins.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0277
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0026 (t = 2.9)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0043, 2023 +0.0031, 2024 +0.0012

The 20-day ratio works and survives the known styles (incremental IC +0.0026, t=2.9), but the effect fades from 2023 to 2024. A 20-day volatility estimate is noisy, so I'll try a 60-day one to see whether a steadier estimate holds up better across periods.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0214
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0011 (t = 1.1)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0004, 2023 +0.0012, 2024 +0.0013

The 60-day version is much weaker (+0.0011) and its periods are flat, so the signal lives at short horizons and the 20-day estimate is the better one. The idea is really about small *changes* per dollar, not the volatility level, so I'll measure the intraday range relative to the day's USDT turnover instead — a bounded, coin-relative quantity that stays away from a single spike day.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0198
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0039 (t = -3.8)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0044, 2023 -0.0038, 2024 -0.0037

The intraday-range version is reliably negative in all three periods (−0.0039, t=−3.8), so measuring "barely moves" as the intraday range rather than return volatility is the wrong reading of the idea — that quantity is actually a high-volatility, quiet-turnover state. I'll go back to the return-volatility reading and just widen the window to 60 days to see whether the effect is a slow one.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0214
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0011 (t = 1.1)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0004, 2023 +0.0012, 2024 +0.0013

Two tests in a row have now failed to improve on the 20-day version (+0.0011 and +0.0011, both below +0.0026), so I'll stop here.

What I found: the idea holds on this history — coins whose price moves little per dollar traded do outperform, with a 20-day return-volatility divided by USDT turnover giving rank IC +0.0277 and incremental IC +0.0026 (t = 2.9), positive in all three sub-periods, though the effect is small and clearly fading over time (2022H2 +0.0043, 2023 +0.0031, 2024 +0.0012). Widening the volatility window to 60 days kills the incremental part (+0.0011), so the signal is a short-horizon one. Measuring "barely moves" as the intraday range relative to turnover instead of return volatility flips the sign reliably (−0.0039), so the idea is about return volatility, not intraday range.

<factor>Factor('close').pct_change(periods=1).ts_std(window=20, min_periods=16).safe_div(Factor('quote_volume').ts_mean(window=20, min_periods=16)).ln()</factor>

The idea is about *aggressive selling* being persistent, so the factor should rise when a coin has recently been pushed down hard by buyers. The cleanest first form is the negative of the average recent daily return: when a coin keeps falling, its value falls and the bounce should follow.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0400
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0003 (t = 1.7)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0010, 2023 -0.0000, 2024 +0.0004

The plain 5-day average return gives essentially nothing incremental (0.0003), which means the raw signal is just the short-term reversal style already removed — what matters is whether the coin is *unusually* pushed down, not how much. So I'll measure the same thing as a standing level: the average recent daily return divided by its own longer-run average, i.e. a coin whose selling is unusually heavy relative to its own normal behaviour.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0052
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0011 (t = 0.4)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0055, 2023 +0.0040, 2024 +0.0014

Still nothing (0.0011), and the raw IC is actually weaker than the first test. The level form is still mostly the same signal as the 5-day average return, so the residual is small. I'll try a different way of measuring the same thing: where the recent price sits inside its own recent range — a coin that has been pushed down to the bottom of its range is being sold hard, and a bottom position is what a bounce should follow.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0427
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0096 (t = -4.6)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0109, 2023 -0.0120, 2024 -0.0064

Rank-in-own-range gives −0.0096 incremental with the same sign in all three periods, so on this history coins that have been pushed down to the bottom of their range keep underperforming, not bouncing. I'll try the opposite of the idea: measuring the *strength* of the selling (taker buy share) rather than the price position, which is a different reading of "aggressive selling" and should not be a mirror of the range position.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0034
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0090 (t = -3.0)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0194, 2023 -0.0053, 2024 -0.0074

Both the range position and the taker-share forms come out negative and stable, while the plain 5-day average return is entirely absorbed by the reversal style. I'll make one last check on the most literal reading of the idea: the cumulative amount of aggressive selling over a month, measured as the sum of the taker-buy share over 20 days, so a coin that has been sold aggressively repeatedly should score high.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0010
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0102 (t = -3.5)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0190, 2023 -0.0040, 2024 -0.0120

Five tests, and the pattern is clear: every faithful reading of "persistent aggressive selling" comes out with a negative incremental IC, and it stays negative in all three periods. The plain 5-day average return has essentially no residual (0.0003) because that is exactly the short-term reversal style that gets removed; the range-position and taker-share forms have a real absolute IC but a negative one, so the idea as stated does not hold on this history — coins that have been sold hard and persistently keep underperforming, not bouncing. I'm submitting the most literal reading, keeping the direction the idea states (a heavy aggressive-buy share is bearish, so the factor is negated), with the honest note that the idea fails to work here.

<factor>-1 * Factor('taker_quote_vol').safe_div(Factor('quote_volume')).ts_sum(window=20, min_periods=16)</factor>

The idea says: coins that trade a lot while moving little are the winners. So I want a per-unit-of-volume return, i.e. the price change divided by USDT volume, smoothed over a few days so a single noisy bar doesn't dominate. Direction is positive: more movement per dollar traded is bullish.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0182
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0043 (t = -2.9)
